overall: Violation found: the Board discussed reasonably anticipated warrant article 28 at its May 12 meeting without listing it on the notice. Three other allegations were declined as not Open Meeting Law issues. No further relief since article 28 failed at Town Meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the May 12 notice omitted Town Meeting warrant article 28, which the Board discussed anyway at that meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law when it discussed article 28 during the May 12 meeting, as the topic was reasonably anticipated yet not included on the Board’s meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board did not allow proponents of article 28 to speak at the May 12 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law, therefore, permits the chair of a public body to decide whether to allow for public participation, and if so, to set limitations on participation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board lacked authority to vote on article 28.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, these allegations would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board took topics out of order at the May 12 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Law also does not prohibit a public body from removing, postponing, or declining to discuss a topic listed on a meeting notice or taking topics in a different order than listed on the notice.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
